utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Would the registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-98-32/1-I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this proceeding is the initial appearance of Mr. Milan Lukic, which is taking place pursuant to Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal. The first thing I think I ought to be clear about is who represents the Prosecution and Defence in this case. For the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Mark Harmon, Frederic Ossogo, and Fergal Gaynor representing the Prosecution. Present also is Lise-Lotte Karlsson, the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Michael Karnavas on behalf of Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Now, Mr. Lukic, could you stand, please. Are you hearing what's being said in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Should any difficulty in that connection develop, you should let me know immediately. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's see if without bending down you can actually communicate with the microphone. I think they probably are good enough, when switched on, to enable you to stand up straight and answer, and if that proves difficult, then you may sit down, but let's see how we get on. Would you state, first of all -- would you state, first of all, please, your full name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 6th of September, 1967.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Foca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Prior to your detention and then transmission to the Tribunal, where did you reside?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I was transferred here, I lived in Argentina. For the last four months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now could you please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, this case has a long history, a long history as far as this accused is concerned and a long history as far as other accused are concerned. Most of that history is well known, and I don't think any particular purpose would be served today by elaborating upon it further. So what I propose to do is proceed straight to the issue that concerns us today, which is the position of the accused - this accused - in relation to each of the counts against him. Now, if I do that, do I require that the whole indictment be read, or is it going to be sufficient in this instance to ask him whether he pleads guilty or not guilty to each of the individual counts by simply referring to what that count is? For example, extermination, a crime against humanity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. First of all, for the record, he has -- Mr. Lukic has been fully apprised of his rights, both while he was in Argentina and while he's here. I have had an opportunity to go over the entire indictment with him, both in Argentina and here. At this time, he knowingly and intelligently and voluntarily waives the reading of the indictment. However, I do understand your request, and I believe that the mere reading of each count and the entering of not guilty on each particular count would be sufficient, and that that would be our position, that we enter a plea of not guilty to each and every count, in fact to the entire indictment, to every single word at this particular point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, just one further matter. Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. There is -- or at least there was an application by the Prosecution to amend the indictment in this case, and that's an amended -- a proposal to amend an already amended indictment. Procedure on that was suspended pending the accused arriving here. For the avoidance of any doubt, it's the indictment which has been established as an appropriate indictment to which he will be invited to plead. I'll come later to the question of the amendment that is now proposed to that indictment, but he will asked in a moment or two to plead to the 21 existing counts on the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But just to be clear, we're pleading not guilty to everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Everything, yes. Now, before I embark on that, Mr. Harmon, is there anything that you want to draw to my attention?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. As Your Honour is going to address the issue of the proposed second amended indictment at a later time, we have nothing to add at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Lukic, would you stand again, please. In a moment, the court registrar will read to you a summary of each count on the indictment, and he will take them one by one, and each time, once he's read the summary, he will ask you whether you plead guilty or not guilty, and you should reply in each instance to that question. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would the registrar now please proceed to take the plea.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Milan Lukic, you have been charged as follows: Count 1: Extermination, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 2, persecution on political, racial, and religious grounds, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 4, murder, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 5, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 6, inhumane acts, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 7, violence to life and person, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 8, murder, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 9, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 10, murder, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 11, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 12, inhumane acts, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 13, violence to life and person, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 14, murder, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 15, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 16, inhumane acts, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 17, violations to life and person, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 18, inhumane acts, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 19, cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 20, murder, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 21, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In view of these pleas of not guilty to each of the charges, I ask the registrar to note that a trial will require to be set in due course. That, of course, is subject to the application which was made in terms of Rule 11 bis to transfer this case away from the jurisdiction of the Tribunal. The motion was suspended, as I understand it, by the Referral Bench, but that suspension was simply until the accused came here. And in view of his arrival here, then that suspension appears to me to automatically be raised, although that's a matter for the Referral Bench rather than me, and the issue is again a live one. Now, Mr. Harmon, I think you know that I take the view that disclosure is not an optional form of procedure that ought to be suspended simply because of an application in terms of 11 bis. So I take it that the Prosecution are now actively engaged in disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We -- two elements that I need to advise the Court about in respect of disclosure: One, we're prepared to make disclosure now. Second of all, Your Honour, there is a -- there was an application for consideration for a proposed second amended indictment. That application was stayed. He is -- until he had arrived in The Hague. Mr. Lukic is now here in The Hague, it is our intention to file next week formally a request for consideration of an amended second indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Remind me of the state of play. There is a motion and there is a proposed amended indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: There is a proposed amended indictment. That was stayed until his arrival.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do we not just need to remove the stay?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We can either do that, that's one issue - it's not entirely clear from going through all of the decisions - that can either take place, or alternatively, we can file formally an application saying now we submit before the Chamber that's seized of the matter an application to amend the present indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the practical issue here is one of a proper representation of the accused. So give me a moment while I ask Mr. Karnavas about that. Are you likely to be counsel in this case, or are you here for the day and gone tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, hopefully not, Your Honour. Hopefully not. I had a power of attorney to represent Mr. Lukic. The Prosecution was aware of this way back in December, as was the Registry became aware of it some two weeks ago. It's my understanding that, based on the 11 bis, at least the application that had been pending, that the Argentinian court transferred Mr. Lukic here on the agreement that he would not be sent to the state court in Sarajevo and that he would remain here or there would be one other option and that would be Belgrade. So I would take it that's why you have this amended indictment that's pending. My suggestion at this point would be not to rush into anything, because I think that it might be fruitful for me to meet with the Prosecution, even at this early stage, and to begin to have certain discussions that, you know, might not make it necessary for that -- that amended indictment to be filed or it may make it necessary for them. So I don't know if I'm asking -- I'm answering your question, but it's my intention to remain in the case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, you've answered that. The reason I thought it might be worth doing something quite quickly on this was that I've, and the Trial Chamber of which I'm part, has recently had to consider a similar motion in relation to a co-accused in the case, and therefore the issues which are similar are alive in our minds. On the other hand, you may not have the benefit of being as well briefed on it. I don't know. But if you were, then I would be inclined to proceed with this, although I'm -- you know, I understand what you're saying to me as well, and I wouldn't like to divert your attention from activities that might turn out to be more productive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I get the gist, Your Honour. I can only say that efforts have been made on my -- on behalf of Mr. Lukic. Unfortunately, we were waiting for him to come here. Now that he is here, perhaps there may be a different approach taken by the Prosecution. I think perhaps they were waiting, thinking that the Argentinian court would not reach the conclusion they did reach, which is why they were reluctant but I can't speculate. I haven't had the opportunity to meet with anybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've given me enough information to decide which option to take, though, and I'm grateful for that. So I think I'll follow Mr. -- Yes, I think I'll follow the course that you originally suggested, Mr. Harmon, and that is leave it to you to file to revive this issue. But that's on the clear understanding that Mr. Karnavas has indicated that he will be speaking to you and, therefore, I'm anticipating he will do that within the next couple of weeks or so, because I really don't want this issue, if it has to be dealt with, to lie dormant for any significant length of time. If we really are to address the issue of amending the indictment, we should do it fairly soon. So can I take it you will speak to the Prosecution within that sort of time scale and allow them to suspend -- they will suspend their action while you do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm prepared to speak with him right after this hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's excellent. Thank you very much. So I'll leave it to you to put in the appropriate motion or filing, Mr. Harmon, once you're satisfied that it's necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We'll be doing that next week. In respect of the question of who represents Mr. Lukic, I am -- received a copy of a decision from the Deputy Registrar. I'm not sure if the Court has a copy of that. It deals directly with the issue of counsel and the decision. It states that Mr. Karnavas will represent Mr. Lukic at his initial appearance and at such other matters as may be necessary until permanent counsel is assigned, effective as of the date of this decision. So obviously discussions with us are -- we're happy to engage in those discussions now, but they will be fruitful with permanent counsel as opposed to counsel that may not be permanent counsel, so I bring that Your Honour's attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It sounds as though Mr. Karnavas is going to apply his ingenuity to remaining permanent counsel in the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No doubt, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And just might I add that my willingness, and I wouldn't say eagerness, but my willingness to meet with the Prosecution is with the full authority and blessing of Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Well, it may be that that's an answer to the question, but I'll leave these matters to counsel to resolve. I don't think it appropriate to do anything. In fact, it may be out of my power anyway to do anything to suspend the period for filing preliminary motions. If you have any to make, then you've got 30 days to make them. Now, is there anything else I ought to deal with, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So far as the accused is concerned, Mr. Karnavas, are you satisfied that he is being properly cared for in the Detention Unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there anything else you think I ought to deal with?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. That concludes today's business. Mr. Lukic, the proceedings are now adjourned and you will remain in the custody of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: at 3.29 p.m.
